I have been farming these 5 mu for 35 years. My father taught me, and I learned the rest by doing it every season. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and talk to the input dealer in town, but honestly, I mostly do what worked last year and what I see the good farmers around me doing.

This year, I am keeping my wheat-maize rotation. I have 2.5 mu for winter wheat and 2.5 mu for summer maize — that is how I split it, same as always.

**Winter wheat:** I will plant the improved variety that my neighbor Lao Zhang used last year. He got good yield, over 500 jin per mu. For fertilizer, I put base fertilizer at sowing: I buy compound fertilizer, about 50 jin per mu of 15-15-15, that is my base. Then I top-dress twice with urea — first at green-up time, about 30 jin per mu, and again at jointing, another 30 jin per mu. In total that is roughly 18 kg nitrogen per mu, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium. I irrigate three times: once after sowing to get it up, once in early spring when it turns green, and once at jointing. The well has enough water for that. I spray herbicide once in spring, and fungicide once around heading if it looks rainy. I do rotary tillage before sowing — the machine comes, costs 40 yuan per mu, but it is worth it. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the spring is decent.

**Summer maize:** Right after wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize seed. I always buy hybrid seed from the dealer — the bag says 4 jin per mu, and I follow that. For fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer at sowing, about 40 jin per mu of something like 16-16-8, then top-dress with urea at the big trumpet stage, about 35 jin per mu. That works out to about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 4 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once after sowing if it is dry, and once at jointing/tasseling — that is the critical time, you cannot miss that. I spray herbicide once after emergence, and insecticide once when I see borers or aphids, usually around the trumpet stage. Tillage is just rotary tillage after wheat harvest, quick and cheap. I expect 600 kg per mu, maybe 550 if the weather turns bad.

I thought about cutting back on fertilizer because prices went up, but last year when I tried using less urea on half a mu, the plants looked yellow and thin. So this year I am going back to my normal rate. Better to spend the extra 100 yuan on fertilizer than lose 200 jin of grain. I have to think about my whole budget — my son sends some money from his factory job, but the farm has to pay for itself.
